data.description:
## Why
The operator highlights a range in a terminal and tells an agent to look at it. Today the agent has to ask for a copy, or read the whole screen and guess. Backlog item: C4.

## Evidence
- c11: no `read-selection` command and no `tab.read_selection` method on origin/main (0ff8887e5e). `git grep read_selection` hits only the Ghostty call below.
- c11: `Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift:5029-5031` calls `ghostty_surface_read_selection` and frees the result with `ghostty_surface_free_text` on the next line. The same pair is in `readSelectionSnapshot` at `:5267-5271`. Both are internal to keyboard copy mode.
- Upstream: cmux #10022 (`436fc1f62e`). Worker-lane method `surface.read_selection` returns `has_selection`, `kind`, `text`, and `base64`, plus `file_path`, `line_range`, or `url` for non-terminal kinds. `ControlCommandExecutionPolicy` marks it `mainThreadCallable: false` (`Packages/macOS/CmuxControlSocket/.../ControlCommandExecutionPolicy+ReadPlane.swift` and the test at `ControlCommandExecutionPolicyTests.swift:229`). CLI is `CLI/CMUXCLI+SurfaceSelection.swift`.
- Research: `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/06-grab-list.md` §1e. Fable marked terminal selection if-time. Astra row 4.5 and `c11-1.0.html` revised it to core for terminals only. Browser and markdown selection are 1.x (Astra 4.5b).

## Scope
In: `c11 read-selection` for a terminal tab, and socket method `tab.read_selection`. Response for a terminal: `has_selection`, `kind` (`terminal`), `text`, `base64`. Off the main-actor dispatch. Empty selection is a successful response with `has_selection: false`, not an error. Targeting matches `read-screen`: explicit `--workspace` and `--tab`, or the caller's own tab.
Out: browser selection, markdown `NSTextView` selection, file preview, `file_path`, `line_range`, and `url`. A document-start script injected into pages. Password-field tracking. Reading the selection on a timer.

## Approach
Register `tab.read_selection` on the socket-worker policy, next to `tab.read_text` (`Sources/SocketHandlers/SocketDispatch.swift:68-69`). One short main hop may copy the Ghostty text if the surface API requires it. Build the JSON off main. Free the `ghostty_text_s` exactly once with `ghostty_surface_free_text`, on the same path as `:5031`. Do not add a second free helper. `LegacyWireAliases.canonicalMethod` already maps `surface.read_selection` to `tab.read_selection`. Accept the legacy method name that way. Do not format scrollback. Cap the copied text at a documented size and set a `truncated` boolean rather than allocating without bound. Update the c11 skill. Register feature flag `read_selection.terminal` if C6's list exists.

## Acceptance criteria
1. On a tagged build, select a known word in a terminal with the mouse, then `c11 read-selection --workspace <ws> --tab <t> --json`. The JSON has `has_selection: true`, `kind: terminal`, and `text` equal to that word. `base64` decodes to the same text.
2. With no selection, the same command exits 0 and returns `has_selection: false` and an empty `text`. The terminal is unchanged.
3. A browser tab returns a clear `not a terminal` error and does not inject script. Confirm with the browser's console or by checking that no selection script was added.
4. A logic or dispatch test asserts the method's execution policy is the socket worker. A DEBUG log from a live call shows `isMain=false` at `socketWorkerV2Response`, aside from the single copy hop if one is required. The response body is built off that hop.
5. Twenty repetitions of select, read, and clear on a tagged build leave the process up, with no malloc or double-free diagnostic in the ghostty log.

## Validation
Policy assertion in `c11-logic` or the existing dispatch tests. `tests_v2` against a tagged build for criteria 1 through 3. Criterion 5 is a short computer-use pass. No soak. This is not on the keystroke path. Do not call it from `forceRefresh` or `hitTest`.

## Dependencies
None. C11-248's method alias is already on origin/main. Feature flag name lives with C6.

## Risks
Typing latency: a read must not mark the surface dirty or call `forceRefresh`. Main thread: do not park this in `processV2Command`. The `invalid_dispatch` guard at `SocketDispatch.swift:957-969` will catch a worker method that lands there. Ghostty pointer: free once. A large selection is truncated, not copied without a cap. Doctrine: this reads what the operator selected in c11. It does not observe other apps. Localization: the no-selection and not-a-terminal strings use `String(localized:)`. Six-locale fill is X1. Public repo: nothing sensitive.

Size: S. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: the primitive is "read the selection in this terminal." It is not a screen classifier.
data.title: Read a terminal selection off the main thread

data.body: Moving scrollback read_text and read-screen off the main actor is C11-295 (ledger B086), after C11-296 teaches that read to start a cold terminal. This ticket stays selection-only. Do not format scrollback here.

# C11-282 validation

Head: `790c98459b836dc754176fc22260ae0f8b40e14b`. Clean, pushed branch `c11-1.0/C11-282-read-selection`. Ordinary merge of main `3786513d84b0d82c2669b2b1b066c54f0d7ada40`: union routing/send/RPC/selection registry entries and preserve both routing and selection documentation sections.

Adds `read-selection` / `tab.read_selection`, terminal-only results, own-tab targeting, explicit-target errors, typed renderer BUSY and `read_selection.terminal` v1. Main resolves the live surface, tries the renderer lock once, copies at most 1 MiB and frees each successful native allocation. Worker clips UTF-8 and constructs text/base64. One monotonic five-second caller deadline includes queueing, capture and encoding; abandoned queued capture is skipped and running capture cleans up without publishing late results. Native formatting/allocation remains synchronous on main and unbounded. The caller deadline and response cap do not bound native work. Root Swift bridge declarations were restored to match C11-294's already-merged native ABI; no engine/submodule edit.

## Checks and identities
- Actual Atlas test action `b7cb5ec3b32c496b842b2071d01aae3a`, clean merge head `b30ce99a17dc5b71e40a8ff5fa5544b51f51976c`: ten tests passed, SelectionReadTests + CapabilityFeaturesTests. Includes actual default five-second abandonment, late running-capture cleanup, one-shot completion, encoding deadline, worker/alias dispatch and UTF-8 below/exact/over-limit boundaries with two/three/four-byte scalars.
- Atlas Debug `5fc36d9e4e504699b135aba96c76b1fb` built and launched that same clean merge head. Subsequent head changes are confined to `tests_v2/test_read_selection.py`; product/test Swift and compiled artifact are unchanged. Captain requires CI green at final head before landing.
- Ghostty `5830d1976eecca0d7dee202aef8fb2338d99ed6d`; Bonsplit `c17c6f41cd71066bda9bec82c54465fe34821c75`.
- Original artifact SHA-256: executable `3abe187162f5fe6341f1a7e0b812b0f7f50bb3769ffba4ce5f007dcac343e1d2`; dylib `5cd35cda888f80bd58b63147f00c6110c5046b7bfae6dc3dd4d0f9e5295775e5`; CLI `a0a77d0e1a5be7612703ed56f2c98932f2a30ca64ad9fa2bc59e5cfacc75a325`. Original artifacts retained privately before remote cache removal.

## Native/runtime evidence
Pre-merge tagged artifact: twenty real mouse select/read/read/built-CLI/clear cycles returned exactly SELECTIONFIXTURE, preserved the selection across reads and stayed alive. No selection, CLI human output/errors, empty/stale window/workspace/tab targets, browser/markdown rejection and hidden legacy alias passed. Browser getSelection call counter remained zero. Final merged artifact: no-selection/discovery plus thirty large native selection reads and built-CLI JSON text/base64 byte parity passed, with no selection mutation. A typed BUSY response was observed during an earlier streaming fixture; the thirty settled samples below all succeeded.

Baseline source `2496017a28e1066a93edb3ad933aa32fe7f62ff6`, Debug `dab6d2cb1ffd43c980040c2618ff2dd3`; same native engine, guest, display, window dimensions and numbered Unicode workload. Both apps used an isolated 50 MB scrollback config. The actually retained selection was 1,045,175 bytes on both artifacts. It remains below the 1 MiB response cap, so these runtime samples report truncated:false. Several-MiB native capture and runtime clipping above the cap are NOT proven; clipping is exercised through the executable logic tests.

All times below are milliseconds, nearest-rank percentiles.

| Path | n | p50 | p95 | p99/max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline native copy caller | 20 | 222.681 | 242.075 | 249.315 |
| Candidate native copy caller | 20 | 228.946 | 254.595 | 271.841 |
| Selection socket caller | 30 | 54.808 | 57.209 | 102.186 |
| Main queue delay | 30 | 0.023 | 0.056 | 47.555 |
| Native formatting on main | 30 | 5.016 | 6.084 | 6.372 |
| Main copy/free | 30 | 0.176 | 0.207 | 0.322 |
| Worker UTF-8/text/base64 | 30 | 1.261 | 1.325 | 1.429 |

DEBUG worker diagnostics show isMain=false. Native timing includes try-lock and formatting together; no separate lock/format estimate is invented. UI-copy timings include driver and pasteboard overhead. Using published C11-270 budget-2 envelopes, the preliminary copy comparison stays below p95 max(baseline*1.2, baseline+5)=290.490 ms and p99 max(baseline*1.25, baseline+15)=311.644 ms. This is not a registered typing/switch soak pass. Typing/switch latency, allocation/leak soak, forced native mutex ownership accounting and a live app-main stall remain integrated-validator work. Production deadline seam tests pass; attempted debugger-based app-main stall was not performed because noninteractive debug attachment was denied. No unbounded native-read claim.

UI ran only in disposable guests: verified native PID/window/display, neutral prompt, exact-window captures, bounded fixture duration, synthesized quit plus confirmation and process disappearance. Both own guests deleted within their leases. Own host tagged app stopped; own remote tag/DerivedData caches removed after retaining artifacts. No installed-skill sync. C11-291 owns translations of admitted English keys.

## Validator scenario
1. Build merged main as a tagged artifact in an isolated guest. Discover terminal selection v1; create a neutral full-size terminal fixture with the committed harness setup phase.
2. Drag the known word using screenshot-derived window-local coordinates; run word and boundaries phases. Expect twenty byte-exact read/read/CLI/clear cycles, no selection success, target errors, unsupported-tab errors and zero browser selection-script calls.
3. Run large phase on actual native scrollback; compare built CLI JSON and base64 byte-exactly. Record the retained native size and truncation. Increase retained native selection beyond 1 MiB for the remaining native clipping proof; do not treat a printed workload size as selected bytes.
4. Measure native main-time and worker timing separately, plus typing/switch latency against the final published C11-270 baseline. Validate forced contention/close-churn and long-run ownership with the C11-294 native harness. Preserve the documented native-on-main residual, use a hard guest lease, and prove dismissal.

# Review C11-282 — FAIL

Head `790c98459b836dc754176fc22260ae0f8b40e14b`. Base `3786513d84b0d82c2669b2b1b066c54f0d7ada40`.

Audit finding 9 holds. Help, skill, and API text say native capture, formatting, and allocation stay on main and are not bounded by the 1 MiB response cap or the five-second caller deadline (`CLI/c11.swift:10246-10248`, `skills/c11/SKILL.md:246`, `skills/c11/references/api.md:55-57`). `read_selection.terminal` is only an id and version. The worker waits on one five-second semaphore (`Sources/SelectionRead.swift:178-186`) and does not hold a lock across the native call, so it cannot deadlock main. Main copies at most 1 MiB and then frees; the worker trims a split UTF-8 scalar after that copy (`Sources/SocketHandlers/SurfaceHandlers.swift:1278-1280`, `Sources/SelectionRead.swift:197-207`). `ghostty_surface_try_read_selection` runs on main in the same turn as the live-surface check, and only `GHOSTTY_TEXT_READ_OK` is freed, once (`SurfaceHandlers.swift:1249-1281`). The blocking `ghostty_surface_read_selection` is not used. The merge kept routing, send, and rpc enabled beside selection, and kept both doc sections.

## Blocking

1. `CLI/c11.swift:3059-3073`. Acceptance criterion 1 and the skill both run `c11 read-selection --workspace <ws> --tab <t> --json` (skill: `skills/c11/SKILL.md:246`). `--json` after the command stays in `trailing`. The guard rejects it with `read-selection: unexpected arguments: --json`, so the command exits non-zero and prints no selection JSON. `jsonOutput` is set only by a `--json` that appears before the command name (`CLI/c11.swift:1744-1747`). The live proof uses that leading form (`tests_v2/test_read_selection.py:162`), so it never runs the acceptance argv. Smallest fix: treat a trailing `--json` as the JSON switch, drop it from `trailing`, and add that argv to the existing CLI assertion.

## Non-blocking

1. `skills/c11/SKILL.md:246`. `--tab tab:2` with no `--workspace` is resolved in the caller's workspace (`CLI/c11.swift:3065-3071`), same as `read-screen`. An agent in another workspace following the example reads the wrong tab, or gets not-found, instead of the operator's highlight. Show `--workspace` and `--tab` together in that example.

## Runtime proof still required

Not the fail reason. C11-282 is outside the risk list, and the validation comment's numbered scenario is enough for the later validator batch. Before that sign-off, Atlas still has to show: the acceptance command above once the trailing `--json` fix is in; a retained native selection larger than 1 MiB so `truncated: true` is proven on the real reader; typing and switch latency against the published C11-270 budget; forced renderer contention and a close that wins the queue, on the C11-294 harness. The recorded 1,045,175-byte reads stay under the cap, and the live main-stall was not run.

C11-282 repair round 1 for review ev_01M3Y49VSTDRRYTJC2TSPRDYGG. Clean head `14c736b2fac706d17d213e51028c76dc53bbba8b`; one commit.

`read-selection` now combines global JSON mode with trailing `--json` and removes that switch before unexpected-argument validation. Other trailing flags still fail. The live word fixture now asserts trailing JSON, and the focused built-CLI fixture executes the exact skill argv `read-selection --tab tab:2 --json` against an isolated synthetic socket.

Targeted check only: full CLI executable compiled remotely from this commit's declared c11-cli Swift source inputs using Swift 5 mode and the build lock; `tests/test_cli_read_selection.py` passed exact skill argv, global JSON, human selected text, empty JSON and unknown-flag rejection. Executable SHA-256 `6a9ec3d00ded58cb5e77006101cfc006e901e0fcc57ef087d89e293d89fb85b8`. No app launch, full suite or installed-skill sync. Earlier native runtime evidence and its stated limits are unchanged. CI pending at the repaired head; captain requires green CI before landing.

# Review C11-282 round 2 — PASS

Head `14c736b2fac706d17d213e51028c76dc53bbba8b`. Delta `790c98459b836dc754176fc22260ae0f8b40e14b..14c736b2fac706d17d213e51028c76dc53bbba8b` only. Prior finding is fixed.

`read-selection` sets JSON output from the global switch or a later `--json`, then drops `--json` before the unexpected-argument check (`CLI/c11.swift:3060-3075`). `read-selection --tab tab:2 --json --bad-flag` still fails and does not send `tab.read_selection`.

The acceptance argv is in the built CLI word assertion: `read-selection --workspace <ws> --tab <t> --json` (`tests_v2/test_read_selection.py:162`). The same trailing switch is what the executed fixture runs as `read-selection --tab tab:2 --json`, plus leading `--json`, human text, empty JSON, and unknown-flag rejection (`tests/test_cli_read_selection.py:49-63`). `--workspace` is parsed off before that check, so it cannot put `--json` back into `trailing`.

## Blocking

None.

## Non-blocking

1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:213-214` runs the other built-CLI scripts and does not run `tests/test_cli_read_selection.py`. A later edit can reject trailing `--json` again while the required CI gate stays green. Add that script beside `test_cli_focus_history.py`.

Screen caller bound is one deadline from `DispatchTime.now() + timeout` with default 5.0 (`SurfaceHandlers.swift:1325-1326`). That same deadline is the resolution wait (`:1333`), the capture wait (`:1373`), and the formatting wait (`:1411`). After the first hop, a past deadline returns before any cold start (`:1367`). The off-main wait is `min(2.0, remaining)` (`:1370`) through `waitForTerminalSurfaceOffMain` (`TerminalController.swift:3723`). Its return is discarded; the surface pointer is read only on the later main hop.

Screen lock acquisition stays `ghostty_surface_try_read_text`. BUSY fails with no allocation (`TerminalController.swift:3814-3820`). Only OK is freed, once, on main, including when the caller has already timed out (`:3823-3827`). `isAbandoned` is checked before each tag (`:3804`) and does not skip a free that OK already owns.

Screen revalidation is the second main hop: workspace identity, the same `TerminalTab`, and `canAcceptPortalBinding` before `terminal.surface.surface` (`SurfaceHandlers.swift:1376-1385`). The worker formats only the copied `TerminalReadBytes` (`:1409-1429`).

Selection caller bound is `SelectionReadOperation`'s five-second deadline (`SelectionRead.swift:13-15`). `beginCapture` refuses a late start (`:20-22`). `wait` times out on that deadline and abandons (`:44-50`). `canPublish` is checked again after worker encoding (`SurfaceHandlers.swift:1317`).

Selection lock acquisition is one `ghostty_surface_try_read_selection` in the same main turn as the live-surface check (`SurfaceHandlers.swift:1251-1267`). BUSY and other non-OK statuses do not free (`:1284-1291`). Only OK defers `ghostty_surface_free_text`, and that defer runs on every OK exit (`:1272-1275`). The main copy is capped at `SelectionRead.byteLimit` (`:1282`, `SelectionRead.swift:59`). UTF-8 clipping and text/base64 encoding run after `wait` (`SurfaceHandlers.swift:1306-1313`).

No lock crosses the other path. Each call builds its own completion (`SelectionReadOperation` or `TerminalReadCompletion`). Those locks cover state only (`SelectionRead.swift:18-19`, `TerminalController.swift:22-24`) and are not held across the native call. The two handlers do not call each other. Both native reads run on main, so one turn's try-lock and free finish before the other turn's try-lock starts. A contended renderer returns BUSY to the later call. Neither path keeps a surface pointer onto the worker.

The deleted conflict side was the branch's old screen prologue (`includeScrollback = v2Bool(params, "scrollback") ?? false`, no timeout). Keeping it would have replaced C11-295. The resolution keeps main's rule: scrollback when `lines` is set or the flag is true (`SurfaceHandlers.swift:1331`).
